profile.reading:
This is a Digital Realty facility at 760 Doug Davis Drive, Atlanta, GA 30354, near Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, per mapping data. This session's fetch of Digital Realty's Atlanta metro property list did not surface a matching named/coded property at this specific address, so no operator-confirmed square footage is reported here.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building is part of Digital Realty's Atlanta metro footprint, concentrated downtown near Georgia Power's service territory, with additional suburban sites in Austell also tracked in this registry. Atlanta has become one of the fastest-growing Southeastern US data center markets, with Georgia Power reporting rising large-load demand from data centers in its integrated resource planning filings. Digital Realty markets its Atlanta properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand, positioning the metro within its global interconnection and colocation platform alongside its larger hub markets tracked elsewhere in this registry.

Digital Realty's FY2025 Form 10-K discloses portfolio metrics by region and metro market rather than per-building specifics for any US facility; this pattern of aggregate, not per-building, disclosure is consistent across every Digital Realty property researched by this registry this session, and is not unique to this entry.

reading.body:
This Digital Realty facility at 760 Doug Davis Drive near Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport has not published its megawatt IT capacity, either in Digital Realty's property pages or in its FY2025 10-K filing. Digital Realty does not disclose power or square footage per individual building; it reports only aggregate figures by region and metro. Whether this campus holds tens of megawatts or several hundred cannot be determined from published operator data.

Digital Realty operates as a colocation landlord, not a compute provider, meaning this building's purpose is to house tenants' accelerators and training clusters, not to run them directly. The operator's portfolio includes 310 data centers worldwide, with 118 US facilities spread across more than 55 metro markets. This Atlanta property sits within Georgia Power's integrated service territory in one of the fastest-growing Southeastern data center markets, where transmission capacity constraints have begun to appear in the utility's planning filings.

Georgia has 33 mapped data center facilities, only 4 of which publish megawatt figures totaling 66.3 MW. This facility ranks fifth by published capacity in the state, but that ranking includes only the four sites with disclosed specs. Its position in Georgia's actual capacity order, and its relevance to state grid planning, cannot be determined without operator disclosure or third-party measurement.
